newsitem.title: JAPAN: LDP exec says bank debenture may be protected-Jiji.
newsitem.headline: LDP exec says bank debenture may be protected-Jiji.

text.p: A senior official of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Party said on Wednesday that creditors holding bank debentures may be protected through the use of various types of government funds, Jiji news agency reported.

"There has been a lot of talk about Nippon Credit Bank but bank debentures may also be considered (for protection by various government funds)," LDP policy chief Taku Yamasaki was quoted as saying by Jiji.

Speaking on the use of additional public funds to deal with Japanese banks' massive bad loans, Yamasaki said there were a variety of public funds other than taxes that can be used, such as funds from the government's fiscal investment and loans programme, special loans by the Bank of Japan and government guarantees, Jiji said.

Yamasaki, in a speech at a hotel in the Tokyo area, also said there is talk that Nippon Credit Bank Ltd should be merged with the government-run Japan Development Bank after it is privatised as a result of the overall deregulation being planned in the banking industry, Jiji said.
However, Jiji quoted Yamasaki as saying that NCB has a capital adequacy ratio of about eight percent and that it will be able to rebuild its business.
Last week, a senior NCB official told Reuters in an interview that there was no reason to worry about the bank's liquidity and denied market rumours that it may be near collapse.
